answer: Require each agent to earn a nontransferable reputation by completing randomly assigned tasks whose outcomes are checked against later evidence and by peers with established histories. A new identity starts with no influence, and only verified work gradually raises its voting or trading limits; suspicious clusters that rate one another are discounted. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: each persona needs time, scarce stake, and independently verifiable contributions, not just a fresh name. Nectar, copper, and a quill can label sample tasks, but labels alone buy no trust.
